summary.text: A 28-year-old woman with a history of a road traffic accident was initially managed at a local hospital with back pain as her only complaint, without loss of consciousness, vomiting, bleeding or external injuries. A posteroanterior chest X-ray showed deformity at T8-T9 that was missed, lateral views were not performed, and she was discharged with persistent back pain.

One month later she returned with persistent back pain. CT of the spine revealed a T8-T9 translational fracture (AO Spine Type C, Denis three-column), left 4th and 5th posterior rib fractures and a left T7 transverse process fracture. She was managed conservatively with a Knight-Taylor brace and referred to the authors center.

At the authors center she walked independently in the brace. Examination showed marked thoracic tenderness at T7 to T9 and an approximately 30 degree kyphotic deformity, with no sensory deficits, 5/5 motor strength, intact anal reflexes, normal deep tendon reflexes and no pathological reflexes. MRI confirmed continuity of the spinal cord, and the transverse section showed pedicle fractures at T8 and T9.

Surgery was planned under general anesthesia, and she underwent in-situ posterior instrumentation with transpedicular screws, rod correction of the dislocation and T8-T9 laminectomy, with three-level fixation selected for the instability; the surgery was well tolerated without postoperative neurological deterioration. Postoperative radiographs showed normal alignment with local kyphosis of 12 degrees, and she was discharged after 20 postoperative days.

Pain was 7 out of 10 pre-operatively and 4 out of 10 at early follow-up at 1 month, with minimal or no pain at the 2-month and 6-month follow-up evaluations. Her neurological status remained intact at follow-up visits after 1 month, and post-operative 2nd and 6th month thoracic spine radiographs were obtained.
